content: Sentara Norfolk General Hospital is a medical facility located in Norfolk, Virginia. It is situated next to Sentara Heart Hospital. This hospital houses the only Level I Trauma Center and burn trauma unit in the Hampton Roads region. Additionally, it serves as the teaching hospital for Eastern Virginia Medical School. Sentara Norfolk General Hospital is recognized as one of the top hospitals in the United States. In 1888, the predecessor to Norfolk General Hospital, known as the 25-bed Retreat for the Sick, was established in downtown Norfolk. At that time, there were fewer than 200 hospitals across the entire country. In 1892, the Retreat for the Sick opened Norfolk's first nursing school. The hospital relocated to a new site in 1896 and was renamed Norfolk Protestant Hospital in 1898. It moved again in 1903 and experienced a fire in 1906, though no lives were lost during the incident. In the 1930s, the hospital was renamed Norfolk General Hospital. In 1967, it became the site of the first open-heart surgery performed in Virginia. In 1981, Elizabeth Carr was born at the hospital, becoming the first baby in the United States conceived through in-vitro fertilization. Furthermore, the first heart transplant in the Hampton Roads region was performed at Norfolk General Hospital in 1989.
